title: Dynamics (part 5)
textbookText: Let’s do the following tasks: i) Have you ever done boating? Go for boating and drive the boat yourself or watch carefully how it is being driven. You throw the water backwards and the boat is seen marching onwards. Think what’s being over there. ii) Have you ever watched the flying rocket in YouTube? A heavy mass of the burnt gas is seen coming out and the rocket heading to the opposite direction. iii) Have you ever fired a gun, or seen someone firing one? Take a gun and fire it as a test. When you fire it, the bullet goes away, while simultaneously you experience a backward push (recoil) due to the reaction force. iv) Consider jumping. When you jump, you first push against the ground, and then you propel yourself forward.
The discovery of a rocket engine exemplifies Newton's third law of motion. The action occurs as the engine expels gaseous fuel backward, while the reaction is observed as the rocket moves forward.
The recoil of a gun represents the action, while the forward journey of the bullet serves as the reaction.
The action of pushing against the ground initiates the jumping motion, while the forward movement is a result of the reaction.
Things to Consider: Newton’s second law is the real law of motion. Why? The second law is written as F = ma = mv−mu t Physics, Grade 11 | 82

If no force is applied, F = 0 ∴ m(v−u) t = 0 Since m ≠ 0, v - u = 0 ⟹ v = u i.e the bodies remain in their own state unless the force is acted upon them. If force is applied, F ≠ 0, ∴ m(v−u) ≠ 0 t ⟹ v ≠ u. i.e, the bodies change the state when force is applied. Hence the first law is deduced from the second law, and hence the second law is the real law of motion. 4.4 Applications of Newton’s Laws of Motion Horse- Cart System:

Fig4.3 An Illustration of the 2nd Law (Horse- Cart System) When a horse pulls a cart, its legs press the ground in an inclined direction opposite to which there is a reaction R. The vertical component of R balances the weight of the horse while the forward horizontal component H acts against the tension on the rope pulling the cart. Since the system moves forward, net force = H –T HC ⟹ H – THC = ma……………………. (4.1) For the cart, Let TCH be the tension on the rope that the horse pulls the cart and f’ be the frictional force on the wheel of the cart acting oppositely. Since the system is moving in the direction of T, net force = TCH- f’. Therefore, for the mass m’ of the cart, TCH – f = m’a……………………… (4.2) Here, the weight w of the cart is balanced by the normal reaction RC on the cart. For the combined system, TCH is cancelled by THC. Therefore, net horizontal force, F = H- f Or, H – f = (m +m’) a ⟹a = m+ m′ H−f Physics, Grade 11 | 83
